display_name: Minna no Shiiku Series 1 - Boku no Kabutomushi (Japan)

slots_and_copies.name: slot_1
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: unknown; only slot id 1 observed via FUN_08022b88(1, ...) in traced caller FUN_0801df08; slot-table entries for other ids (incl. the slot-0 target of Writer A, FUN_08022b24) are not resolvable from static data

checksums.name: record_sum8_complement
checksums.formula_detail: stored_byte = (~(sum(header[0..27] with byte[0x17] zeroed) + sum(payload[0..payload_len-1]))) & 0xFF. Equivalently, sum(header_as_stored) + sum(payload) == 0xFF (mod 256) for any valid record.

io_driver_functions.notes: 8-bit additive sum: first 0x1c (28) bytes at param_1 (header), then param_3 bytes at param_2 (payload). Wraparound char accumulator.

Unverified 'fast' writer: raw-copies a 28-byte header and a variable-length payload into SRAM via FUN_0802cb44, computes a checksum via FUN_08022ae0 but does not appear to store it; only identified caller passes slot=0, src=EWRAM 0x02000000, size=0x3000. No byte evidence this path ever executed in the two available .sav samples (entire file outside the 0x301c-0x3089 window is untouched 0xFF).

Verified writer: builds a 28-byte header (zeroes byte 0, optionally memcpy's a 22-byte ROM default template into bytes 1-22 when 'fresh' flag param_2==0), computes the sum8 checksum, stores its one's complement at header byte 0x17, then writes header+payload via FUN_0802cc7c (write+verify+retry up to 3x). This is the writer that produced the single real record found in saves/cap-01-future-1.sav.
Low-level raw copy used only by the unverified writer path; sets a bus/wait-state control word then delegates to func_0x0802ccc0 for the byte transfer.
Sets SRAM wait-control bits (*_DAT_0802cbe0 |= 3) then performs a tight byte-copy loop. Used as the 'write' half of the verified writer's retry wrapper.
Structurally parallel to 0x0802cb44 (same wait-control idiom); used as the read-back/verify half of the retry wrapper.

Write-then-verify wrapper, retries up to 3 times (for (i=0;i<3;i++) { write(); verify(); if (ok) break; }). Called twice per FUN_08022b88 invocation: once for the 28-byte header, once for the payload.
Generic memcpy (word-at-a-time with 4-byte alignment check, byte fallback). Used to seed 22 header bytes from a fixed ROM default template when the 'fresh record' flag is set.
Generic memset (word-at-a-time with alignment check, byte fallback). Used by the only traced caller to zero-fill the 82-byte payload buffer immediately before saving.

caller_chains.trigger_context: Unknown in-game trigger; FUN_0801df08 has no identified caller in the static call graph (reached only via an unresolved indirect/jumptable dispatch per the many 'UNRECOVERED_JUMPTABLE' warnings throughout decompiled.c). It zero-fills an 82-byte RAM payload buffer, then calls the verified writer with slot=1, fresh-template flag=0, that same buffer, size=0x52.
ram_fields_updated: global 28-byte header staging buffer at _DAT_08022bf4 (template bytes 1-22 copied in, byte 0 zeroed, checksum byte 0x17 computed)
caller_chains.how_mapped: Found by grepping decompiled.c for literal references to the address 0x08022b88; FUN_0801df08 was the only call site. Confirmed by exact byte match against saves/cap-01-future-1.sav: 28-byte header length, 82-byte all-zero payload, and checksum byte all match the traced code and the Python-recomputed checksum.

caller_chains.trigger_context: Unknown in-game trigger; FUN_08007ab4 has no identified caller in the static call graph. It directly calls the unverified writer with slot=0, src=EWRAM 0x02000000, size=0x3000 (12288 bytes).
ram_fields_updated: unidentified 0x02000000-region EWRAM buffer (producer not found in the 246-function trace set)
caller_chains.how_mapped: Found by grepping decompiled.c for literal references to the address 0x08022b24; FUN_08007ab4 was the only call site. NOT confirmed by byte evidence: no .sav sample shows any write consistent with a 12288-byte bulk transfer; both files are 0xFF outside the single 110-byte window attributable to the other caller chain.

fields.name: record_type_or_flags
fields.update_mechanism: Zeroed as part of a 4-byte store (*_DAT_08022bf4 = 0) at the start of FUN_08022b88, prior to any template copy.
fields.evidence: Write mechanism proven in decompiled.c; semantic meaning (version/type/flags) is speculative since only a single value (0) has ever been observed.

fields.name: template_block
fields.update_mechanism: memcpy'd verbatim from a fixed ROM default template (_DAT_08022bf8) via FUN_0802e77c whenever FUN_08022b88's 'fresh' flag (param_2) == 0. The param_2 != 0 reuse code path, which presumably preserves/updates live game data here instead of the template, was never exercised in the available 2-sample evidence.
fields.evidence: Byte-for-byte match against a verbatim ROM-template memcpy is CONFIRMED_STATIC at the mechanism level, but no byte evidence exists of this block ever containing anything other than the static template, so per-field game semantics (e.g. any individual sub-value being a stat/currency/species id) remain unverified hypotheses.

fields.name: checksum
fields.update_mechanism: puVar1[0x17] = ~FUN_08022ae0(header, payload, payload_len); one's complement of the sum8 checksum over the 28-byte header (with this byte temporarily zeroed) plus the full payload.
fields.evidence: Independent Python recomputation against saves/cap-01-future-1.sav reproduces the exact stored byte (0x15); see save-format report section 4 for full script and output.

fields.name: reserved_unknown
fields.update_mechanism: Included in the 0x1c-byte header range passed to the write-verify wrapper (func_0x0802cc7c), so it IS written every save, but its in-RAM source value at _DAT_08022bf4[0x18..0x1b] was apparently already 0xFF at save time in this sample, so the write was a no-op in effect.
fields.evidence: No writer sets these bytes to anything other than their pre-existing value in the one available sample; could be intentional padding or incidental buffer residue.

fields.name: payload
fields.update_mechanism: The only traced producer, FUN_0801df08, zero-fills this RAM buffer with FUN_0802e864 (memset) immediately before calling FUN_08022b88 to save it. No other producer of this buffer's contents was found in the 246-function decompiled corpus.
fields.evidence: 82-byte length, RAM buffer address, and all-zero content all match decompiled.c and the real .sav bytes exactly; however since content is always zero in available evidence, no sub-field structure within the payload can be determined.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Flip one bit of the stored checksum byte (XOR 0x01)
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: If the loader validates this checksum, expect a visibly different load outcome (reset-to-default, refusal, or re-templating) vs. an unmutated file. Falsifies whether the checksum is actually checked on load, which static tracing could not confirm (no load-side caller identified).

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Change a single template byte, e.g. file offset 0x301e from 0x60 to 0x61, then repair checksum
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: If this byte is live game data, expect a visible UI/stat change after reload; if dead/unused padding, expect no observable change. Tests the HYPOTHESIS confidence on the template_block field.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Set all 82 payload bytes to 0xAB instead of 0x00, then repair checksum
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Any crash, garbage display, or stat change confirms the payload is actively read; no observable change would suggest this record/slot is not yet consumed by game logic as of this capture.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Set the 4 reserved bytes to 0x00 instead of 0xFF, then repair checksum
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Tests whether the game structurally validates or ever reads these bytes; a rejection or crash would reclassify them from UNKNOWN to CONFIRMED_VERIFIED as meaningful padding/guard bytes.

open_questions: What in-game action or dispatch path actually invokes FUN_08007ab4 and FUN_0801df08? Both are unreferenced in the static call graph and only reachable via unresolved indirect/jumptable calls.
What are the slot-table entries (_DAT_08022b70 for Writer A, _DAT_08022bfc for Writer B) for slot ids other than 1, including the slot-0 target used by Writer A?
Do the 22 template header bytes ever differ from the fixed ROM default, i.e. what does FUN_08022b88's param_2 != 0 ('reuse existing record') path actually write?
What is the semantic/gameplay meaning, if any, of the template block's internal values and of the 82-byte payload region?
Are header bytes at relative offset 0x18-0x1b (file 0x3034-0x3037) intentional reserved/guard bytes or incidental RAM buffer residue?
Is the stored checksum actually validated on load, and if invalid, what is the game's fallback behavior?
Is there truly no redundancy/backup copy, or does a second copy exist at a slot-table offset we have not yet sampled?
